class_guess: Bell eats counter variant (W5-5's table, 2 cells changed): hub defect + unary counter, ternary transfer
summary: 100-block segments with one hub marker: each round moves 3^(k+1) blocks across the hub and adds 1 to a unary counter
mechanism: The tape is runs of 100 blocks joined by markers: one hub marker 0 (W5-5's 0001 defect, mirrored), 101 separators, and a unary counter (101)^c at the right end. HUB(k), exact: the head zigzags left through (101)^c, makes 3^(k+1) short trips at the hub (each moves one 100 block across it), then adds one 101 to the counter; k = number of 101 separators right of the hub.

When the hub's right segment b drops below 3^(k+1), the outcome branches on b and the neighbours (99 events to 1e9): the hub becomes a 11 marker, moves, or the head sweeps to the left edge. Once per deep cycle (88 cycles to 1.55e11) the head reaches the left edge; then the counter drains one 101 per long trip while inner hubs work in older segments, which later freeze (58, 106, 1452, 393, 165, 338, 838, 12269, 41798).

No halt to 1.55e11. Head windows (radius 4-10) stop changing after 1e7 steps, but plain NGramCPS fails for n = 2-20. Halting needs A or D to meet 111 moving right (A1 = 0RD, D1 = 1RF, F1 = halt); the real tape has 111 only at deep sweeps, where C passes it moving left. 1 of 2,000 random segment tapes halted, and it was malformed.

template.module: W5-5's own .v (KILLED_HALT): bellpart, round = callw + bellpart, base-4 digit lemmas abs0/abs1/absm/pass2/callw_inc
template.diff: A0: ours 1RB, W5-5 1RE; E1: ours 1RD, W5-5 0LD (W5-5's table started in its D, in our naming)
template.note: Same 3-cell words and the same bell-with-defect round, mirrored: our hub marker 0 is W5-5's 0001 defect. W5-5's defect moves 1 block per round and feeds a signed base-4 counter; here it jumps 3^(k+1) blocks and the counter is unary (101)^c. HUB(0) is W5-5's round with a unary counter; none of the digit lemmas carry over. W5-5's checked-runner route needs a halt, and none is in sight.

strategy: Route 1 (NONHALT, preferred): look for a closed regular language on 3-cell words (block CPS / CTL with the gap-token vocabulary); it would not need the residue arithmetic. Route 2: model the exhaustion branches and the deep cycle exactly, then look for a closed residue table. Stop if the exhaustion law is a pseudo-random residue map.
risks: Exhaustion branches on b mod 3^(k+1) and re-cuts segments; frozen segment lengths and counter values look irregular (Collatz-type signal). A 111 met by A or D moving right halts, and 111 does occur at deep sweeps.
Plain NGramCPS fails for n = 2..20, so any regular invariant must use phase or block structure; it may not exist.
Deep cycles get long (2.9e10 steps per cycle at 1.5e11), so long-run evidence grows slowly.
